examples.solution_text:
a. Bus was most popular: its tallest column represents $35$ students. Walking was least popular: its shortest column represents $10$ students.

b. Read the bus and car values from the vertical scale.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}35-30\\&=5\end{aligned}$

$5$ more students travelled by bus.

a. The temperature rose from $11^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at 9 am to a peak of $23^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at 12 pm, then fell to $19^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at 1 pm.

b. Compare the increases over the equal one-hour intervals.

$\begin{aligned}14-11&=3\\21-14&=7\\23-21&=2\end{aligned}$

The greatest increase was $7^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, from 10 am to 11 am. The temperature fell during the last interval.

c. No. The increases were $3^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, $7^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $2^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, followed by a decrease.

a. Supported. The levels were $80\%$ and $20\%$, and $80=4\times20$.

b. Unsupported. $80-20=60$, so the total fall was $60$ percentage points.

c. Supported. $80-50=30$ and $50-20=30$, so both displayed intervals had a fall of $30$ percentage points.

The vertical axis measures finishing time. B's tallest column represents $24$ seconds, the longest time, so B was slowest.

For the same distance, the fastest student takes the least time. C took $16$ seconds, the shortest time, so C was fastest.

coverage.summary: Authored four worked examples covering all six distinct assessed methods. Each has separate editable question and solution fields, an unshaded editable graph, and supported solution styling through the renderer. Checked calculations, axis scales, units, gutters and answer separation. Practice and quiz content remain unchanged and were read solely for method classification. Independent review and final-size visual verification remain pending.

examples.derivation: The columns represent Car 30, Bus 35, Walk 10 and Bike 25. Bus has the greatest frequency; walking has the least. The difference is 35−30=5 students. This follows the mapped booklet transport comparison. The continuation calculation includes the required phantom equals gutter.

The plotted temperatures are 11, 14, 21, 23 and 19°C at consecutive hourly measurements. Changes are +3, +7, +2 and −4°C. Temperature rises to its peak at noon, then falls. The greatest increase occurs from 10 am to 11 am; equal hourly increases are unsupported. These use the supplied booklet trend and interval-comparison methods. Independent equations correctly have no phantom equals.

The columns show battery levels of 80%, 50% and 20%. Since 80=4×20, claim a is supported. The total decrease is 80−20=60 percentage points, so claim b is unsupported. Both hourly decreases equal 30 percentage points, supporting claim c. Testing multiplicative, difference and equal-change claims matches the mapped home-price exercise.

The finishing times are A 18, B 24, C 16 and D 21 seconds. All students ran 100 m. B took the longest time and was slowest; C took the shortest time and was fastest. This directly follows the mapped booklet running-time claim.
